The RevenueNow framework operates under a dual-logic structure: (1) picks are a trust-building mechanism, not a monetizable asset, and (2) tools form the core revenue engine. The trust magnet (T) is defined by the public track record of picks (P) and user calibration (C), modeled as T = f(P, C). Tool economy (U, V, R) is a linear combination of usage and value, R = Σ(U_i × V_i). The value ladder (L) defines tiers of access, each with a feature set F, such that S(L) = g(F). These primitives form a coherent system where trust drives adoption, tools drive revenue, and value tiers optimize user progression. Failure modes include: (a) T < 0.5 leads to abandonment, (b) U below threshold stalls MRR, and (c) L = 1 prevents upgrades. The system assumes independence between picks and revenue, and that tool utility scales with user sophistication.
